The question of who has the right to govern Crimea is a contentious and complex issue. In 2014, Crimea was annexed by Russia, following a controversial referendum in which the majority of Crimean residents voted to join Russia. Ukraine and most of the international community, however, consider Crimea to be part of Ukraine and the annexation by Russia to be illegitimate.

In terms of international law, Crimea is still considered part of Ukraine, as recognized by the United Nations and most countries around the world. However, Russia continues to govern the region and has established it as a federal subject of the Russian Federation.

Ultimately, the question of who has the right to govern Crimea is a matter of ongoing dispute and is likely to remain unresolved for the foreseeable future.
